title: May openings: @Joe Weinberg  Unrehearsed Shakespeare:  @Joe Weinberg ...
transcript: Theatre fans, do not believe the myth that summer is a slow time for theatre in New York. Here are a bunch of shows opening this summer that I think should be on your radar. this is kind of a follow up to a video I did with shows opening in May which you should definitely check out in the caption cause a bunch of those are running into the summer too. and in the true spirit of summer I'm gonna front-load this video with a lot of Shakespeare and outdoor theatre so if you're not interested in that you can skip to this timestamp starting off with Tempest Tossed this is an adaptation of the Tempest that is like site specific and it incorporates chamber music I saw this same company do a version of Romeo and Juliet that I really liked but this is the one I may be most excited about in this whole video so the Public Theatre is remounting NAATCO’s production of Henry VI. they essentially condensed all three plays into two parts and I saw this same production back in 2018 and I loved it. If you're not familiar with the Henry VI plays this would be a great intro to them. of course that's not the only Shakespeare being done at the Public this summer they have Shakespeare in the park first off starting with Romeo and Juliet and later in the summer they're doing The Winter's Tale and for their mobile unit where they travel around to different parts of the city they're doing as you like it But the public isn't the only company who does outdoor Shakespeare Classical Theatre of Harlem is one of my favorite summer traditions and this year they're doing Othello also definitely keep your eye on Barefoot Shakespeare Company they haven't announced this yet but toward the end of every summer they do their Unrehearsed series where they do a Shakespeare play unrehearsed but it's a lot more fun than it sounds they like, turn it into a competition I did a whole video about it which I'll link in the caption also. also kind of at the end of the summer into fall is Moliere in the park they're doing Don Juan and finishing off the outdoor section of this video we have the Circuit which, as you can see is described as an “immersive silent disco ballet” and apparently it's inspired by the play of La Ronde. next we have a few revivals that I'm really looking forward to they're doing a La Cage at Encores which I've actually never seen performed live Sting is renting out the Met Opera House to do a reworked version of his musical, The Last Ship which I was a big fan of when I saw it on Broadway. There’s a revival of this play from the 70s called Are You Now or Have You Ever Been which is about Mccarthyism and this production has a rotating cast of celebrities. next we have the Whoopi monologues which if I understand correctly I think they've taken some of Whoopi Goldberg's theatrical solo show work and adapted it for multiple actors including Kerry Washington and my beloved Kara Young. We have a couple of interesting new musicals opening this summer including Giulia which is written by and starring Jennifer Nettles inspired by a true story about a woman who worked as an apothecary in the 17th century one I'm really excited for is the Potluck by Cesar Alvarez who is an alternative indie musical theatre artist who hasn't had a show in New York in a while I really like their work and this one has like a historical component to it it's about a group of protesters who were killed in the 70s but Alvarez also has a personal connection to them if I understand correctly. of course we have some exciting new plays as well starting with Birthright from the writer of Eureka Day and it's about a reunion of friends who went on Birthright together and if you're not Jewish and you don't know what Birthright is uh Google it The Saviors a new play from the same writer director team as Well, I'll let You Go and this one is about a pair of altar boys. we have the second and third shows of Clubbed Thumb’s SummerWorks series also one of my favorite summer traditions. Derangements is by Nadja Leonhard-Hooper who some of you might know as one of the co writers of the musical Hole! I'm just gonna read this description cause it's great: “two girlfriends catching up over dinner have their lives changed in a flash” “maybe it's the 80s but maybe it's just gas” after that is the Family Dog “in which Whitney returns to her childhood home” “to say goodbye to the pet who replaced her” “miracles abound, some in meatball form” and we have a new play called The Loved Ones at Irish Rep which is a family drama and it has a really exciting cast including Donna Lynn Champlain from Crazy Ex Girlfriend Alana Raquel Bowers, Marianne Plunkett the final three on this list are all solo shows that look really cool we got Big Feelings, where you're sort of placed in the role of a first grade class and the teacher is speaking to you. Are You Mad at Me a show from the fringe about social anxiety and people-pleasing and finally I really should have included this in my May openings video but we have the return engagement of Can I Be Frank I saw this back in the fall it's a really great show where Morgan Bassichis looks at the comedian Frank Maya and it's sort of about the legacy of queer comedians. I'm gonna call it there but that's not even all of the theatre opening this summer so if I missed anything you're excited about feel free to put it in the comments
